Draw from Posterior Predictive Distribution for DOAS Bayesian Models

Source: R/ppc.R
posterior_predict.Rd

Simulates replicated datasets from the posterior predictive distribution of a fitted doas Bayesian model. For double-observer sectors, observations are simulated from the multinomial capture-recapture process conditional on posterior draws of latent abundance and observer detection probabilities. For single-observer sectors, observations are simulated from a binomial detection process.

Usage

posterior_predict(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'doas'
posterior_predict(
  object,
  n_draws = NULL,
  type = c("count", "detected", "both", "joint", "obs1", "obs2"),
  drop_unsurveyed = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted doas model object with method = "Bayes".

...

Additional arguments (currently unused).

n_draws

Number of posterior predictive draws to simulate. If NULL (default), all available post-warmup draws across chains are used.

type

Character string indicating what quantity to predict:

  • "count" or "detected" (default): Total unique individuals/groups detected at each sector (comparable to object$data$total_count).

  • "both" or "joint": Joint detections \(y_{12}\) in double-observer sectors.

  • "obs1": Observer 1 detections (\(y_1 + y_{12}\) in DO sectors).

  • "obs2": Observer 2 detections (\(y_2 + y_{12}\) in DO sectors).

drop_unsurveyed

Logical. If TRUE (default), unsurveyed sectors (which have no field observations) are omitted from yrep and attr(yrep, "y").

Value

A matrix of class c("doas_yrep", "matrix") of dimension n_draws x n_sectors, with attributes "y" (observed vector), "sector_id" (sector identifiers), and "target" (predicted quantity).

Details

The returned matrix yrep has dimensions n_draws x n_sectors and includes the observed data vector as attr(yrep, "y"), making it directly compatible with bayesplot::ppc_* functions.
